conclusion: Shift/natural-extension structure does not select a unique one-coordinate record-content basis; an invertible shift-commuting recoding can mix adjacent records.

base_factor_projection_test.interpretation: C is a shift automorphism but not an isomorphism OVER the declared base process. Natural-extension uniqueness with its factor map is stronger than shift-only uniqueness.

refined_conclusion: Shift alone does not select record content, but the natural extension as an extension over a fixed base factor does distinguish the base records up to base-system relabeling. It still does not identify history coordinates with spatial sites.
